title: R-Codes application data document (consolidated, draft-2026-10-24)
description: Facts a proposal supplies as data, generated from the base application schema and the fact vocabularies of Chapters 2, 3, 4 Part 1 and 4 Part 2 (FACTS.md). Property paths are the dotted fact names rules read (site.verge.path_or_road_offset_m is site -> verge -> path_or_road_offset_m). A fact that is absent or null is unknown, never zero; every numeric fact should have a facts_meta entry keyed by its dotted name. dwellings is either an array of per-dwelling objects (flattened as dwellings.0.bedrooms, with dwellings.count) or an object of development-wide summary facts that describe the least compliant dwelling or a share of dwellings (dwellings.min.*, dwellings.max.*, dwellings.*_pct; Chapter 4 Part 1 and Part 2 apartments). x-used-by lists the rule IDs that read a fact; x-vocabulary the chapters whose FACTS.md lists it. Objects are open: properties not listed here are allowed.

region.description: Perth and Peel regions per Chapter 1 2.5.2

x-notes: site.area_m2 in element 1.1 (Table 1.1b, C1.1.4 161 m2 threshold) and 1.2 (C1.2.1 15% 'per site'): the site of the dwelling being assessed (A1 'site' for a grouped dwelling). Whether C1.2.1 is tested per dwelling or across the development is ambiguous (register ch3-009).

site.area_m2, building.roofed_area_m2 (C3.1.1): for a grouped dwelling, the dwelling's own site (land it occupies plus all areas for its occupants' exclusive use, no share of common property; A1 'site', register ch3-043; C4.1.2(i)). Not the parent lot. Run C3.1.1 once per dwelling, or supply the dwelling with the highest site cover.
site.area_m2 in elements 1.2 and 4.1: the whole development lot (apartments have no individual sites). Table 1.2a 'lot size' is read as this.

site.area_m2, building.roofed_area_m2 (C3.1.1): for apartments the whole lot, or parent lot under a strata scheme, on which the dwellings stand (Appendix A1 'SITE', multiple dwelling or apartment limb), not a per-dwelling site as in Chapter 3.

has_pedestrian_access_leg.description: a pedestrian access leg is required (C3.7.8)

communal_street_soft_landscape_width_m.description: width of soft landscaping within the communal street (C3.7.15(iii))

has_public_realm_frontage.description: the site has a street or public realm frontage (A3.2.1 applies; A3.2.2 where false)

corner_sightline_clear_0_75m.description: walls, fences and structures within 1.5 m of the street corner are no higher than 0.75 m (A3.8.7-r1)

local_housing_mix_requirement.description: a local housing strategy or relevant local planning instrument sets dwelling mix objectives, proportions or targets for the site (A4.8.1(a)/(b) switch)

mixed_use_area_designated.description: the site is in a mixed use area designated in the local planning framework; scopes A4.14.1

dwelling_count.description: number of grouped dwellings on the site
x-notes: proposal.dwelling_count: the number of grouped dwellings in the development, not counting ancillary dwellings. It is the "total number of dwellings" in the visitor ratios (C2.3.3, C2.3.7) and drives the 5-dwelling waste plan note (C2.4.3-r1) and the 10-dwelling universal design trigger (C2.7.1). Verify whether ancillary dwellings count.

proposal.dwelling_count: the number of apartments in the development. Drives C1.3.1 (more than 10), C2.1.7 (more than 10), C2.3.3 (exceeding 20), the visitor and bicycle ratios (C2.3.5, C2.3.7, C2.3.7-r1), C2.7.1 (10 or more), Table 2.8a (1-19 / 20 or more), and is the C4.1.1 divisor. Verify whether ancillary (dual key) dwellings count.

Per-dwelling facts (proposal.bedrooms, parking.spaces, parking.garage_carport_spaces, building.storage.*, building.upper_pos.*, proposal.internal_floor_area_m2): each describes the dwelling being tested. Where a development has more than one dwelling type, supply the least compliant dwelling, or run one application per dwelling type.

Per-dwelling facts (proposal.bedrooms, parking.spaces, parking.garage_carport_spaces, building.storage.*, building.upper_pos.*, proposal.internal_floor_area_m2): each describes the dwelling being tested. proposal.internal_floor_area_m2: in C2.7.2 the accessible dwelling seeking the variation; in C2.9.1 the small dwelling under the concession.

proposal.retained_dwelling (C3.7.2(i) exception, C3.7.12(i) reduction): an existing dwelling is retained on the site. This chapter has no retained-dwelling element, but those two clauses still refer to retaining an existing dwelling.

universal_design_level.description: A4 or Livable Housing Australia level

seeks_universal_design_site_area_variati.description: the application seeks the gold-level universal design site area variation under C4.1.6 or C4.1.7 (C2.7.1)
x-notes: proposal.seeks_universal_design_site_area_variation: in this chapter the variation is under C4.1.5 or C4.1.6 (the proposal section row above cites C4.1.6 or C4.1.7, the Chapter 3 numbers).

proposal.dwellings_universal_design_pct: percentage of all dwellings built to silver level or better (gold counts). For a whole number of dwellings, pct >= 20 is the same test as count >= 20% of dwellings rounded up (C2.7.1 footnote 1).

reduced_small_dwelling_count.description: of proposal.reduced_site_area_dwelling_count, how many are small dwellings (C2.9.1); C4.1.4 and the C4.1.6 50% cap count small dwellings only (C4.1.1)

communal_street_setback_m.description: setback of a dwelling to a communal street or battleaxe leg

x-notes: building.internal_boundary_treated_as_lot_boundary (C3.4.6): true when every C3.4.1 to C3.4.5 test (setbacks, upper-storey wall length, boundary structures and boundary walls) is met at each internal site boundary between grouped dwellings on the same lot, read as if it were a lot boundary. A single setback number (building.internal_boundary_setback_m) cannot express this, because the required setback depends on wall height and C3.4.4 allows nil-setback walls.

separation_same_lot_m.description: separation between buildings on the same lot (C3.4.6)
x-notes: building.separation_same_lot_m (C3.4.6): the least separation between the facing walls, measured as for a lot boundary setback (minor projections up to 0.75 m excluded, C3.4.1(i)).

x-notes: building.upper_level_overlook_street (C3.6.1): true when upper-level balconies and/or windows overlook the street and public domain areas. The rule applies only where building.storeys >= 2. The public open space limb is C3.6.1-r1, which uses building.upper_level_outlook_to_pos where site.adjoins_public_open_space.

building.ground_floor_apartments_separate_entry (C3.6.2): true where every ground-floor apartment fronting the street has its own pedestrian access from the street, and also true where no ground-floor apartment fronts the street.

x-notes: building.boundary_wall_storeys (A2.4.1-r2): 0 where no wall is built to a side boundary.

boundary_wall_length_pct.description: boundary wall length as % of the boundary (Table 2.1 note 4, two-thirds)
x-notes: building.boundary_wall_length_pct (A2.4.1-r3): each boundary wall's length as a % of the boundary it abuts, the larger where walls are on both sides (note 4 read per boundary; verify).

street_setback_m.description: minimum setback to the primary or secondary street (A2.3.1)

building.side_setback_m (A2.4.1): the least side setback of the building excluding any wall built to the boundary that is assessed as a boundary wall under A2.4.1-r2 and -r3. Otherwise a Table 2.1 boundary wall would always fail the 4 m side setback at R80 to MR1.

plot_ratio.description: gross floor area divided by site area (A2.5.1)
